<thought>The observed mass spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic envelope: a dominant monoisotopic peak followed by a series of peaks spaced ~1.003 Da apart with rapidly decreasing intensities (≈17 % for M+1, ≈1.6 % for M+2, etc.). This pattern matches the natural ^13C/^12C distribution for a molecule containing many carbons and does not display the characteristic 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) M+2 patterns. No other element’s isotopic signature is evident. Therefore, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the spectrum.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
